title: Storage: wiring backends through the typed callbacks
preamble:
# Storage: wiring backends through the typed callbacks

How an integrator wires a storage backend (SQLite,
Redis, Postgres, an in-process map, an HA-recorder
DB, anything) into libds via the cache callbacks and the
sample callbacks.
Pairs with the language-side contract
([LSTO])
which describes what authors see; this doc is what
the integrator implements.

The libds surface is callback-only — there is no
embedded storage backend, no wire to a storage adapter,
no protobuf. Each integrator picks a backend that
fits their deployment and writes a thin adapter
between libds's typed callbacks and the backend's
API.

## What this is not

- Not a backend recommendation. Pick whatever fits
  your deployment.
- Not a backend implementation. libds doesn't
  ship one.
- Not the language-side surface. See LSTO for the
  three-plane model + author contract.
- Not a runtime implementation guide for the planes.
  Code under `runtime/src/libds/` documents itself
  via the public header (`libds.h`) and the
  contract docs (`IDSP`, `IARC`); this doc covers
  the integrator-facing surface.
